questions.q: What does an asset book determine for every asset that belongs to it?
options: Only the physical location of the asset
The ledger, depreciation calendar, and default rules it inherits
The vendor who sold the asset
Nothing — books are purely cosmetic labels
questions.explain: An asset book is a container tying assets to a specific ledger, a depreciation calendar, and default accounting and calculation rules.

questions.q: Which book class is used first for every new asset?
options: Tax book
Budget book
Corporate book
None — assets don't need a book until retirement
questions.explain: Every asset starts life in a corporate book, the primary book used for financial statement reporting.

questions.q: How is a tax book typically populated with asset data?
options: Manual entry identical to a corporate book
Mass copy from an associated corporate book
Direct import from the General Ledger
Tax books cannot contain asset data
questions.explain: Tax books are populated by a mass copy process that copies corporate book asset data and transactions, rather than manual entry.

questions.q: What is a budget book used for?
options: Recording actual depreciation for financial statements
Filing the company's tax return
Forecasting future depreciation and capital spending without affecting real books
Storing retired assets permanently
questions.explain: Budget books let a company plan and forecast depreciation and spending without touching actual corporate or tax book data.

questions.q: Why is book setup typically one of the first tasks in an Oracle Fusion Assets implementation?
options: Because books expire after one year and must be recreated
Because every asset added later inherits the book's ledger, calendar, and default settings
Because books determine which vendors can be used in Payables
Because book setup has no effect on later configuration
questions.explain: Since every asset added to a book inherits its ledger, calendar, and defaults, getting book setup wrong propagates that mistake to every asset that follows.
